title: Meridian Utilities certification roadmap and log retention clarify
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 / ISO27001 scope, trust portal artifact access, KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood), RBAC/SSO SAML flow, and log retention needs. Meridian requested 365-day audit log retention for regulatory reporting, EU data residency for a subset of workloads, and proof of periodic pen tests. Agreed next steps: invite Meridian to Trust Portal, share SOC2/ISO artifacts, deliver proposed evidence extract procedure, and schedule a focused KMS integration call.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (Meridian Security Manager), Priya Nair (Meridian Compliance), Ethan Moore (Meridian Cloud Ops)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call please?
[00:08] Jordan (Meridian): Jordan here.
[00:10] Priya: Priya on the line.
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan.
[00:14] Alex: Great. Samira and Diego from our security/infra side are with me. Goal today is to walk through our SOC 2/ISO posture and the trust artifacts, plus clarify your log retention and KMS needs.
[00:30] Samira (Redwood SE): I'll kick off with what we keep in the Trust Portal — SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO 27001 cert scans, pen test summaries, and our control matrix mapping to common frameworks. Note sometimes the auto transcript calls it 'trust center' but we call our portal 'Trust Portal'.
[00:48] Priya: Nice. Can you confirm frequency — is the SOC 2 Type II the last 12 months rolling? We need the latest for our internal audit.
[00:58] Diego (Redwood): Yes, Type II is annual with a 12‑month coverage period; we upload the report and supporting control evidence pointers. Some supporting artifacts are downloadable, others are view-only for privacy.
[01:15] Jordan: View-only is fine but our audit team will need downloadable evidence for cloud config snapshots. What's the process?
[01:24] Samira: We can provide a scoped evidence extract. Typically we do a CSV export for config-type artifacts and zipped logs for infra evidence. For security reasons some raw items are redacted — like exact API keys — but config manifests and timestamped console logs are included.
[01:40] Ethan: How long do you keep audit logs? Our regulator requires 365 days for certain operational events.
[01:47] Alex: Out of the box we keep 90 days in the hosted product, 365 days is available as an add-on or included with Dedicated/private deployments. We can also stream logs to a customer S3 bucket for long-term retention.
[02:02] Priya: If we stream to S3, can it be EU-region only? Data residency is important for us, some assets must remain in EU.
[02:11] Diego: Yes, we can pin workloads to eu-west-1 region and configure log exports to a customer-managed EU bucket. For Private deployments we support on-prem options as well.
[02:25] Jordan: Good. About KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM?
[02:33] Samira: We support CMKs with KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). HSM-backed keys are supported on enterprise/private plans. Quick note: sometimes the transcript mis-hears KMS as 'K M S' in auto text.
[02:47] Ethan: What's the flow for encrypting model artifact at rest — is it per-tenant disk encryption or per-object?
[02:55] Diego: We do envelope encryption: service-keys encrypt objects, and those service-keys can be wrapped by your CMK. You can choose to rotate the CMK per policy. For Dedicated & Private we also support customer-controlled HSM.
[03:10] Alex: Also we'll provide our KMS integration guide and a sample Terraform snippet.
[03:18] Priya: Great. On the controls mapping, can you show how Redwood maps to SOC 2 CC and ISO controls? Our GRC tool needs the mapping CSV.
[03:28] Samira: We maintain a controls matrix that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 common criteria and ISO 27001 clauses. We can export as CSV. We'll highlight which controls are in-scope for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[03:40] Jordan: Do you include compensating controls for multi-tenant hosting?
[03:44] Diego: Yes, the matrix flags compensating controls and shows the evidence we maintain.
[03:50] Jordan: Ok.
[04:00] Alex: Let's talk about SSO and provisioning. Are you using SAML? SCIM?
[04:05] Ethan: We're SAML2 for SSO and looking into SCIM for user provisioning.
[04:09] Samira: Redwood supports SAML SSO with IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, plus SCIM v2 for user/provisioning sync on Dedicated & Private. For hosted we have SCIM in beta for enterprise customers.
[04:26] Priya: How granular is RBAC? Our auditors want role separation — dev vs ops vs security.
[04:32] Diego: RBAC supports built-in roles (admin, developer, observer) and we support custom roles on Dedicated/Private. You can restrict by org, project, and model access.
[04:42] Jordan: Any logs of admin actions? We need immutable audit trails for changes to RBAC and KMS key usage.
[04:49] Samira: Yes, audit logs capture admin operations — role changes, key rotate events, and config updates. We sign and timestamp logs; we can stream to your SIEM or object storage. For immutability you can ingest into write-once media or cloud object lock configs.
[05:05] Alex: Quick FYI there are occasionally small mis-transcribes — 'KV cache' might show up wrong — ignore that in the portal.
[05:12] Priya: Understood. Pen test evidence — do you publish full reports or executive summaries?
[05:18] Diego: We publish an executive summary in the Trust Portal and provide a redacted full report under NDA. Customers on enterprise contracts can request the full test output via secure transfer.
[05:30] Jordan: And frequency? Annual?
[05:33] Samira: Annual plus ad-hoc before major releases.
[05:38] Ethan: We want to run a quick smoke benchmark for latency and privacy for EU pinned workloads. Would you be able to run a scoped test or provide test endpoints?
[05:47] Alex: We can give a short-lived scoped token and EU endpoints for your bench. We'll coordinate rate limits to avoid affecting other tenants.
[05:55] Priya: Is there an SLA around availability and RTO for Dedicated versus Hosted?
[06:01] Diego: Hosted has a standard SLA with 99.9 for API availability; Dedicated has higher committed SLOs per contract and optional on-call. We'll share the SLA PDF.
[06:12] Jordan: Great.
[06:20] Samira: I'd like to walk through an example of the evidence export process — say you need proof of encryption configuration for a specific model deployment.
[06:28] Priya: Yes please.
[06:30] Samira: (screen-share described) The export includes timestamped config JSON, the KMS key thumbprint, the CMK ARN (redacted in public doc), and signed log snippet with the admin action that attached the CMK. The CSV ties to SOC 2 control CC6 for change management.
[06:52] Jordan: Perfect. The auditors typically ask for links to the control mapping.
[06:56] Samira: We'll send the CSV with control IDs mapped to your internal GRC references.
[07:04] Alex: Any concerns on your side we haven't covered?
[07:08] Priya: One question — evidence retention: if Redwood keeps 90 days but we need 365 for the regulatory artifacts, is the recommend approach to stream logs to our S3 daily and keep raw evidence there?
[07:20] Diego: Yes that's the pattern we recommend. We provide a managed export job that can be scheduled daily, weekly, or ad-hoc. The export includes a manifest file for auditability.
[07:32] Ethan: For the export manifest, will it include checksums?
[07:35] Samira: Yes, each artifact has an SHA256 checksum in the manifest.
[07:40] Jordan: About the Trust Portal invite — can we create accounts for our external auditors with view-only privileges and time-limited access?
[07:49] Diego: Yes, you can invite external users and assign time-limited roles. We support guest links and expiration policies.
[07:58] Alex: Let's capture agreed actions — we'll invite your auditor as a guest with view-only then follow up.
[08:05] Priya: Also can we get the pen test executive summary and SOC 2 bridge letter?
[08:10] Samira: Yes, both will be uploaded or shared as attachments.
[08:15] Alex: Quick note on procurement: if you choose Dedicated, we can include longer log retention and HSM in the SOW. For hosted you can add the log export + EU pinning as config.
[08:29] Jordan: Cost question — is there a per-GB cost for storing logs in Redwood’s longer retention?
[08:34] Diego: For hosted extended retention there's a storage surcharge; for streaming to your S3 costs are your bucket charges and nominal export fee. We'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[08:46] Priya: Fine.
[08:50] Alex: Any other product questions?
[08:53] Ethan: On SCIM, how frequent is the delta sync?
[08:57] Samira: SCIM can be scheduled every 5–15 minutes depending on plan.
[09:02] Jordan: Good.
[09:10] Alex: Ok we'll open up for Q&A.
[09:18] Priya: For evidence mapping to ISO 27001 annex A, do you have the clause numbers (A.5–A.18) aligned in your matrix?
[09:27] Samira: Yes, we map to Annex A clauses and provide crosswalks to our controls. We'll annotate which controls are partially satisfied due to shared responsibility in hosted mode.
[09:40] Jordan: Shared responsibility is key — can you provide wording that we can paste into our vendor-risk register about which controls remain with Meridian?
[09:49] Diego: We'll prepare a vendor responsibility summary (one- page) that calls out customer responsibilities: identity lifecycle, data classification, and retention policies.
[09:58] Alex: Let's capture next steps and then we'll wrap.
[10:03] (discussion continues with scheduling details)
[10:18] Alex: Action items recap...
[10:25] (transcript noise, brief crosstalk)
[10:40] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:42] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up with the materials.
